name: box
description: Use this to draw a box around one thing in an image, such as "the damaged package" or "the person climbing the fence". Returns the top-left corner `x1`, `y1` and the bottom-right corner `x2`, `y2`, `present`, `confidence` (that the box overlaps the true box by at least half, an intersection over union of 0.5), and the `image` looked in with its `width` and `height`, with the call's `cost` in USD. Costs one request. `present` is the probability that the thing is in the image at all and `confidence` the probability that the place is right if it is: act on the answer when both are high, and hand the image to a person when either is low. Needs at least one image; with two or more, `image` names the one to look in by its id (a reference by number, "Picture 2", goes in the instructions). `model` is optional: leave it out for the default model, or pass `decisionnode-flash` for the faster, lower-cost tier.

instructions.description: What to draw the box around, such as "the damaged package".
instructions.title: Instructions

images.description: The images, at least one: the one to look in, and any others the instructions refer to. Up to 16 images every question can see, within the model's token limit, each with a short, meaningful id (`receipt`, not `2`). The instructions refer to an image by its id in backticks (recommended) or by its number from 1 in this order ("image 2", "Picture 2"). Each is {id, url} with an https URL, {id, data, media_type} with base64 data, or, on the local server only, {id, path} for a file on the user's machine. On the hosted server the base64 data of one call is limited to about 3 MiB in total; send larger images by https url.

id.description: Unique within the request; a short, meaningful name (`receipt`, not `2`). The model sees the image as `Picture <n> (<id>):`, so the instructions can refer to it by this id in backticks (recommended) or by its number.

url.description: An https URL the API fetches.

path.description: A file on the user's machine. Local server only; the hosted server refuses it.

image.description: The id of the image to look in (a string). Needed with two or more images; with one, that one. A reference by number ("Picture 2") goes in the instructions.

units.description: pixels (the default): pixels of the image as sent. normalized: fractions of the width and the height, from 0 to 1.

state.description: What to judge: a string, or any JSON value (an object with named fields works well). The model sees only this, the question and any images. Leave it out for a question that stands on its own.
state.title: State

model.description: The model id. Leave it out for the default, `decisionnode-moe`; `decisionnode-flash` is the faster, lower-cost tier. The `models` tool lists the ids your key may use.

x1.description: The left edge of the box (its top-left corner's x).

y1.description: The top edge of the box (its top-left corner's y).

x2.description: The right edge of the box (its bottom-right corner's x).

y2.description: The bottom edge of the box (its bottom-right corner's y).

confidence.description: The probability that the box overlaps the true box with an intersection over union of 0.5 or more, if the thing is there.

present.description: The probability that what the instructions describe is in the image at all. Under a low `present` the place is only a best guess for something probably not there.

image.description: The id of the image looked in.

cost.description: What the call cost, as the API booked it, in USD: `usd` (the amount booked), split into `model_usd` and `boosters_usd`, and `free_tier` (true when the free tier covered the model's part).

safety.description: Present only when the safety check flagged a category for this key: each category's probability and the `flagged` categories.
